newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG rejects rebel claim of mercenary attack.
newsitem.headline: PNG rejects rebel claim of mercenary attack.

text.p: The Papua New Guinea defence force on Tuesday rejected a secessionist rebel charge that mercenaries had launched a mortar attack on Bougainville.
"This is a rumour, it is part of the BRA (Bougainville Revolutionary Army) propaganda," Papua New Guinea Defence Force Chief-of-Staff Colonel Jack Tuat told Reuters.
Tuat said the town of Arawa, which the rebels said was the target of the attack, was in fact held by government troops and that there were no mercenaries on Bougainville island.
"Arawa is regarded as a pacified area and we are looking after the livelihood of the people there," Tuat said.
"Why would we attack our own town?" he said.
However, Tuat said a "skirmish" may have occurred outside Arawa between government troops and rebels.
The rebels' Bougainville Interim Government said on Tuesday that mercenaries fired three mortars towards the Bougainville capital Arawa in the centre of the island on Monday.

"The BRA intelligence network and observers said the mortar bombardments destroyed a large area but no casualties have been reported from the ground as yet," said the Bougainville Interim Government in a statement issued in Sydney.

The rebel statement also said mercenary-led government troops had landed on Bougainville, 800 km (500 miles) northeast of Port Moresby, and had taken up position near the island's giant Panguna copper mine.
Rebels forced the closure of the mine in 1989. Papua New Guinea on Sunday said it wished to buy back foreign interest in the mine and reopen it, providing compensation for landowners.
Papua New Guinea has hired 40 mercenaries through British-based Sandline International and says they are training government troops for a mission to Bougainville.
Tuat said all Sandline International personnel were training troops on the country's mainland outside the town of Wewak.
The use of mercenaries has attracted diplomatic criticism from Australia, New Zealand, Britain, the United States and South Africa.
